source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν προσφάτως φωτισθέντα προσάγεσθαι ἐν τάγματι ἱερατικῷ. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Προστάζει ὁ παρών Κανών, νά μὴ γίνωνται Ἱερεῖς ἢ Κληρικοὶ οἱ νεοφώτιστοι, παρευθὺς μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα. Ὅρᾳ καὶ τὸν π΄. Ἀποστολικόν.
thought_title: The newly baptized must not be ordained at once
orientation: The council is issuing its canons; this one addresses who may be brought into the clerical order.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the not needing the recently baptized to be brought forward in the priestly order. Interpretation. The present Canon commands that the newly baptized not become Priests or Clerics, immediately after the baptism. See also the eightieth Apostolic.

choices.why: The glossary maps φωτιζόμενοι to 'those being baptized'; here the aorist participle means one who has just received baptism.
The term literally means 'newly enlightened' but refers to the recently baptized; 'newly baptized' is the plain English sense.
The phrase denotes the clerical rank or order; 'priestly order' keeps the literal noun 'order' and the adjective 'priestly'.
The source distinguishes two terms; keeping both as capitalized nouns preserves the distinction in the canon's command.
The phrase is temporal and emphatic; 'immediately after the baptism' renders both the adverb and the article with the noun.

pass_b_english: Concerning the rule that one recently baptized must not be brought forward into the priestly order. Interpretation. This present canon commands that the newly baptized must not become Priests or Clerics immediately after the baptism. See also Apostolic Canon 80.
